function.name: get_weather_forecast
function.description: Retrieves the weather forecast for a specified location and date range. The forecast includes temperature, precipitation, and wind speed. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which the weather forecast is requested, in the format of 'City, Country' (e.g., 'London, UK').

start_date.description: The start date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-01').

end_date.description: The end date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-07').

units.description: The unit system in which to return the weather forecast data.

include_details.description: Specifies whether to include detailed forecast information such as humidity and visibility.

**How Turbonomic Helps Unilever Leverage AI for Multi‑Cloud Observability** | What Turbonomic Provides | How It Benefits Unilever | Key Features | |--------------------------|--------------------------|--------------| | **Unified AI‑Driven Optimization Engine** | Combines workloads, resources, and business value into one decision engine that automatically moves or scales services across AWS, Azure, GCP, and on‑prem environments. | • Real‑time analytics
• Predictive capacity planning
• Automated remediation actions | | **Observability & Telemetry Aggregation** | Collects metrics, logs, and events from all clouds into a single pane, giving Unilever a holistic view of performance, cost, and compliance. | • Cross‑cloud dashboards
• Custom alerts based on business KPIs
• Root‑cause analysis | | **Policy‑Based Governance** | Lets Unilever define policies that reflect corporate objectives (cost control, SLA adherence, security). Turbonomic enforces them automatically. | • Cost‑budget enforcement
• Compliance checks (PCI, GDPR)
• Role‑based policy scopes | | **Self‑Healing Automation** | Detects anomalies (CPU spikes, memory leaks) and takes corrective action without human intervention. | • Auto‑scaling triggers
• Workload relocation
• Resource reclamation | | **Cost Visibility & Forecasting** | Provides granular cost attribution per workload, project, or business unit, enabling Unilever to see where money is spent and predict future spend. | • Tag‑based cost allocation
• Forecasting models
• Savings recommendations | | **Integration with Native Cloud APIs** | Uses official SDKs/APIs to pull telemetry from CloudWatch, Stackdriver, Azure Monitor, etc., and pushes decisions back via native interfaces. | • API connectors
• Event‑driven workflows
• Secure credential management | ### Why Turbonomic Adds Value Over Native Cloud Tools | Aspect | Native Cloud Tool (AWS CloudWatch / GCP Operations / Azure Monitor) | Turbonomic | |--------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|------------| | **Scope** | Monitors only within its own ecosystem; limited cross‑cloud visibility. | Unified view across all clouds + on‑prem. | | **Decision Logic** | Basic alerting and manual scaling; requires DevOps to act. | AI‑powered autonomous decision engine that recommends or executes actions. | | **Optimization Granularity** | Focuses on infrastructure metrics; lacks business‑value mapping. | Maps performance to business value (e.g., revenue impact), enabling value‑based decisions. | | **Automation** | Limited auto‑remediation; often requires Lambda/Functions scripts. | Built‑in self‑healing, auto‑migration, auto‑rebalancing. | | **Cost Management** | Billing dashboards provide cost but not actionable savings insights. | Generates concrete savings plans, tracks realized vs. projected savings. | | **Governance** | Policies exist but are usually applied at the cloud level (IAM roles, tags). | Policy engine spans multiple clouds, integrates with corporate governance frameworks. | | **Data Integration** | Each platform stores telemetry separately; integration requires custom pipelines. | Native connectors ingest data from all clouds into a single repository. | | **User Experience** | Multiple consoles, each with its own UI/UX. | Single unified dashboard, consistent UX across clouds. | ### Practical Impact for Unilever 1. **Reduced Total Cost of Ownership (TCO)** – By continuously optimizing resource usage, Unilever can cut idle compute costs across AWS, Azure, and GCP by up to 30–40% (typical industry benchmarks). 2. **Improved Service Reliability** – Self‑healing reduces downtime incidents, directly protecting e‑commerce sales during peak periods. 3. **Accelerated Digital Transformation** – With automated migration and scaling, Unilever can move workloads faster to the most cost‑effective cloud region or provider. 4. **Enhanced Regulatory Compliance** – Policy enforcement ensures that data residency and security controls are maintained across all clouds. --- **Bottom Line:** Turbonomic extends beyond the native monitoring and alerting capabilities of GCP, AWS, and Azure by providing a single AI‑driven platform that aggregates telemetry, applies business‑centric policies, and autonomously optimizes workloads across all clouds. For Unilever, this means lower costs, higher reliability, and tighter alignment between IT operations and corporate strategy—all while keeping the complexity of multi‑cloud environments under control.
